title: Trapping Sets of Detector Error Models
authors: Michele Pacenti, Nithin Raveendran, Bane Vasic
abstract: Message-passing decoders are among the most promising candidates for scalable quantum error correction, yet their behavior in the low-error-rate regime remains poorly understood under realistic circuit-level noise. In this work, we introduce a systematic framework for identifying the graph structures that govern decoder failures and for using them to predict the resulting error floor. We apply exhaustive trapping-set enumeration directly to the detector error model of a bivariate bicycle code and test all low-weight fault configurations supported on the resulting structures. This converts the analysis of extremely rare logical failures into a finite structural search, avoiding the prohibitive cost of direct Monte Carlo simulation. We evaluate the framework on three iterative decoders with substantially different architectures and decoding heuristics. Remarkably, for \texttt{RelayBP}, the resulting prediction accurately reproduces the simulated error floor; for the others, it remains within the same order of magnitude. Despite their differences, leafless elementary trapping sets capture a substantial part of the low-weight error-floor contribution for all three decoders. Moreover, each decoder admits failures caused by fault configurations well below the correction capability implied by the circuit-level distance, revealing a substantial gap between code distance and practical iterative-decoding performance. These results establish trapping-set analysis as a practical framework for predicting error floors, exposing the structural weaknesses of iterative decoders, and guiding the joint design of decoding algorithms.
summary: This paper develops a systematic framework to predict the error floor in quantum error correction codes by analyzing their detector error models. It uses exhaustive enumeration of 'trapping sets'—specific graph structures causing decoding failure—to bypass costly simulations. The results establish trapping-set analysis as a powerful tool for guiding the joint design of both quantum codes and decoding algorithms.
main_problem: The work aims to understand the structural weaknesses of message-passing decoders used for quantum error correction in the low-error-rate regime.
main_result: Trapping-set analysis provides a practical framework that accurately predicts the achievable error floor for iterative decoders, revealing performance gaps between code distance and actual decoding capability.
method: The authors introduce a systematic framework involving exhaustive enumeration of 'trapping sets' directly applied to the detector error model (DEM) of QLDPC codes.
model_or_system: The study analyzes Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) codes under circuit-level noise, modeled via their Detector Error Model (DEM). The analysis focuses on message-passing decoders like RelayBP and ImpulseBP.
key_observables: Error floor (minimum logical error rate), Trapping Sets (TSs), low-weight fault configurations, and the gap between code distance and practical performance.
important_parameters: Low-error-rate regime, circuit-level noise, weight of error patterns, and the structure of the Tanner graph associated with the DEM.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on restricting the search to 'leafless elementary trapping sets' (LETSs), which is motivated by classical LDPC literature but its applicability to QLDPC/DEMs is noted as an assumption.
paper_structure: The paper systematically defines the DEM structure based on fault origins ($D(r)$, $A(r)$, $U(r)$) derived from circuit scheduling, then applies graph theory algorithms (like dpl-search) to enumerate LETSs, and finally evaluates these sets against various iterative decoders.
why_interesting: The methodology of using structural analysis (trapping sets) to predict performance limits is highly relevant for designing robust quantum computation protocols by identifying inherent hardware/algorithmic weaknesses.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
